Carried-forward amendment (still in force): an earlier canonical change rewrote src/pricing/total.js (DELIVERY=3, FREE_DELIVERY_FROM=100, HANDLING=2, deliveryFor, orderTotal) and test/total.test.js, so test/total.test.js is an edited file, not a run-only surface — its case "the discounted amount is what decides free delivery" builds a fractional intermediate (110 lines, loyal 15% off -> 93.50, +3 delivery +2 handling = 98.50, +20% tax = 118.20) and asserts 118 only because whole-pound rounding truncates it; that single assertion becomes 118.2 (comment should read: the total is 118.20). The tax exemption fires only for all-digital baskets — the changed tests "tax is charged on a standard order" and "a mixed basket is still taxed in full" confirm STANDARD_RATE still applies to ordinary baskets — so the 20% tax step in the total.test.js free-delivery case is unaffected and 118.2 remains the correct new expectation. test/tax.test.js is added as a run-only verification surface guarding that assumption. export and search remain untouched.

plan.objective: Orders that contain only digital goods should not be charged tax
expectedSchemas: order.lines[].digital (new boolean marker on an order line; a line is digital when line.digital === true)
expectedTests: test/tax.test.js
test/total.test.js
plan.intent: Approach unchanged; one assumption re-verified against the canonical advance. The advance touched src/pricing/total.js and test/total.test.js (DELIVERY, FREE_DELIVERY_FROM, HANDLING, deliveryFor, orderTotal), neither of which this plan edits — src/pricing/tax.js and test/tax.test.js remain the only files to change, so no file assumptions are stale. Implement in taxFor(amount, order): return 0 when order.lines is non-empty and every line has digital === true, otherwise apply the existing STANDARD_RATE (20%) exactly as today. The empty-lines guard is now load-bearing rather than defensive: total.js calls taxFor(withCharges, order) where withCharges = discounted + deliveryFor(discounted) + HANDLING, and test/total.test.js:28 asserts orderTotal({lines: []}) === 6 (5 of charges taxed at 20%); a vacuous "all lines are digital" for an empty basket would return 5 and break that test. The other total.test.js cases use lines without a digital marker (undefined, not true), so they stay taxed and untouched. Note the consequence to accept: because the exemption is applied to the full charged amount, a wholly digital order pays no tax on its delivery/handling either — waiving delivery for digital orders is out of scope here. Run the full `node --test` suite so any interaction through orderTotal with the new delivery/handling logic is caught.
